source: Same reasoning as e^z, for any positive real base != 1
caption: Power(2, ComplexInfinity) is Indeterminate, the same direction-dependence as e^z
A base between 0 and 1 is just as direction-dependent: (1/2)^z -> 0 one way, -> infinity the other
A symbolic or non-positive-real base is left unevaluated -- not decidable without knowing more about the base
Power(1, ComplexInfinity) is 1 -- 1 raised to any power is identically 1, decidable without a limit at all

source: DLMF 4.2, via e^z unbounded along +Re(z), 0 along -Re(z)
caption: Power(ExponentialE, ComplexInfinity) is Indeterminate: e^z grows without bound in one direction and vanishes in the opposite one, so no single limit exists at the undirected infinity -- this is also Exp(ComplexInfinity), since Exp(z) canonicalizes to Power(ExponentialE, z)
